item.title: Dodging Bombs and Drones, This Postman Still Delivers
item.summary: Oleksiy Klochkovsky has driven mail and parcels around the front line in Ukraine for four years. He keeps one ear tuned for danger from above.

item.title: As War Chills Economy, Dubai’s Most Vulnerable Bear the Cost
item.summary: Migrant workers in the United Arab Emirates, whose hospitality industry has been hit hard by the war with Iran, are facing furloughs, pay cuts and even repatriation.

item.title: As Bahrain Cracked Down Amid War, a Death in Custody Sparked Outrage
item.summary: The body of a man accused of spying for Iran, Mohammed al-Mousawi, showed signs of torture, witnesses said. The U.N. has called for an investigation.

item.title: Europe Is Desperate for More Energy. Can Norway Come to the Rescue?
item.summary: The war in Iran has once again exposed Europe’s energy vulnerability. A friendly source at home would seem to be ideal. But it’s not that easy.

item.title: Rubio Hosts Israel and Lebanon for Rare Meeting Shadowed by U.S.-Iran War
item.summary: The gathering ended with encouraging words, even as Israel continued to refuse to halt its military campaign against Iran-backed Hezbollah in Lebanon.

item.title: Trump’s Blockade Risks Upending an Emerging Détente With China
item.summary: In a thinly veiled critique of the war in Iran, China’s leader said the world could not risk reverting “to the law of the jungle.”

item.title: How China’s Weapons Transfers to Iran Have Evolved Over Decades
item.summary: China has denied claims this month by U.S. intelligence that it might have shipped arms to Iran. In recent years, China has supported Iran with dual-use parts.

item.title: Russian Oil Revenues Nearly Doubled in March
item.summary: The surge in revenue provided a critical lifeline for Moscow, which has struggled to fund the war in Ukraine amid record-high deficits.

item.title: Ship ‘Spoofing’ in Strait of Hormuz May Compound Confusion
item.summary: A new pattern of deceptive activity by some vessels around the critical waterway suggests the new American blockade is changing how some ships linked to Iran are behaving.

item.title: [PENDING_TRANSLATION] How Peter Magyar Defeated Viktor Orban, a Former Ally, In Hungary’s Election
item.summary: For years, Peter Magyar was a loyal ally of Viktor Orban, the far-right Hungarian leader. Then he changed sides — and defeated his former boss in a landslide victory on Sunday. Does he represent real change?
